109.title: Agile Process
rows: Create user stories with clearly defined acceptance criteria to ensure alignment on expected outcomes
Ensure alignment on expected outcomes. Everyone knows exactly what "done" looks like before work begins
Copilot can suggest story templates, phrasing, or examples, but context-specific input is required.
Review and prioritize the product backlog to decide which features to be prioritized
Decide which features deliver the highest business value. Team always works on what matters most.
Requires business understanding and stakeholder decision-making.
Conduct a bi-weekly sprint retrospective to identify what went well, what needs improvement, and actionable next steps
Reflect on the sprint to identify what went well, what didn't, and how the team can improve
Estimate effort for each task using story points or hours to support realistic sprint planning and capacity allocation
Support realistic sprint planning and capacity allocation. Team commits only to what it can actually deliver
Business understanding and complexity analysis required
Document key discussion points, decisions, and action items during huddles and share meeting notes promptly with the team
Capture key discussion points, decisions, and action items during huddles. Share meeting notes promptly after each session
Facilitate daily standup and evening huddle sessions to synchronize the team on progress, plans, and blockers
Round-robin: Done/Doing/Blocked. Synchronize the team on progress, plans, and blockers. PM escalates immediately
Conduct bi-weekly sprint planning sessions to define the sprint scope, set priorities, and commit to deliverables
Capacity review, backlog grooming, story pointing, sprint goal. Define scope, set priorities, and commit to deliverables.
Define the Sprint Goal, a clear objective for the sprint
Set a clear, focused objective for the sprint. Gives the team one shared target to rally around.
Measure and report team velocity at the end of each sprint to support future capacity planning and forecasting
Track story points delivered per sprint. Support future capacity planning and forecasting with data, not guesswork.
Collect and document stakeholder feedback from sprint review and update backlogs accordingly
Capture input from sprint review and feed it back into the backlog. Stakeholder voice shapes what gets built next.
Give Business owners a clear monthly view of progress, risks, metrics, and outcomes.
Assess long-term trajectory with stakeholders. Realign strategy, review KPIs, and plan ahead.
Maintain daily task updates in ADO — including status changes, hours logged, and any blockers
Update status changes, hours logged, and blockers. Ensure task statuses reflect current state; no stale items.
Track and follow up on retrospective action items to ensure continuous improvement is carried forward into the next sprint
Ensure improvement actions are carried forward into the next sprint. They don't just get discussed — they get done.
Maintain and update project documentation (wiki, runbooks, process docs)
Keep wiki, runbooks, and process docs current. Preserve knowledge so the team isn't dependent on any single person.
Collaborate with the FA team to schedule and complete external reviews within the defined timeline
Schedule and complete external reviews within the defined timeline. Prevent reviews from becoming delivery blockers.
Collect and document stakeholder feedback from sprint review and update backlogs accordingly
Capture stakeholder input post sprint review. Update backlog priorities accordingly to reflect new learnings.
Identify and document dependencies between stories or with other teams early in planning
Map cross-story and cross-team dependencies upfront. Avoid surprises and last-minute bottlenecks.
Conduct Backlog Grooming/Refinement sessions (mid-sprint) to keep upcoming stories ready
Clarify, split, and refine upcoming stories. Keep them sprint-ready so the next cycle starts without delays.
Close the sprint formally — move incomplete items back to the backlog, update ADO status, and prepare for the next sprint cycle
Move incomplete items back to the backlog, update ADO status, and prepare for the next sprint cycle. Clean close every time.
Maintain and update the sprint board in real time to provide visibility into task status (To Do → In Progress → Done)
Provide visibility into task status (To Do → In Progress → Done). Ensure the board reflects reality at all times.
Identify, escalate, and resolve blockers promptly to keep the sprint on track and prevent delivery delays
Flag blockers in standup, escalate immediately, track to resolution. Keep the sprint on track and prevent delivery delays.
Map Feature Dependencies across the Product Backlog
To identify technical or sequence-based blockers between different user stories early, ensuring the development team works on high-priority tasks in the correct order.

Relationship Extraction: Analyzes natural language in user stories to automatically flag keywords (e.g., "requires," "depends on," "after") and suggest link types between tickets.

Sequence Optimization: Simulates different development paths to recommend the most efficient order of operations, preventing developers from starting a task only to find its prerequisite is missing
Perform a Bottleneck and Blockage Root-Cause Analysis
To identify recurring friction points in the "In Progress" or "Review" stages of the board and implement structural changes to improve lead time.
Analyzes pull request comments and ticket history to detect if bottlenecks are caused by technical complexity, unclear requirements, or personality-driven review friction.
Audit Automated Test Coverage per User Story
To verify that the ratio of automated unit/integration tests scales proportionally with new feature development, ensuring the "Done" state reflects true stability.

Code-to-Story Mapping: Correlates new code lines in a PR with the specific User Story ID to verify if corresponding unit test files were created or modified.

Gap Identification: Scans the logic of a new feature and suggests missing test cases (e.g., edge cases or boundary values) that a developer might have overlooked
Profile Environment Stability and Deployment Readiness
To analyze the frequency of failures in Dev/Stage environments to identify infrastructure instability that prevents the team from reaching a "shippable" state at the end of the cycle.

Log Clustering: Aggregates thousands of lines of deployment logs to identify the "Signal in the Noise," pinpointing whether a failure was a transient network issue or a recurring configuration conflict.

Predictive Alerting: Analyzes trends in Dev/Stage failures to predict a "Deployment Red Zone" before the team attempts a production release.
Perform a Definition of Ready (DoR) Gap Analysis
To evaluate incoming user stories for missing technical requirements (e.g., lack of API specs or clear acceptance criteria) before they enter the sprint to reduce mid-sprint churn.

Automated Gatekeeping: Acts as a pre-sprint filter by scanning user stories against a DoR checklist and flagging those missing critical artifacts like API contracts, UI mockups, or Acceptance Criteria.

Drafting Support: If a story is flagged as "Not Ready," the AI can automatically generate draft acceptance criteria or boilerplate API specs based on the story's title and description.
